name: v19.2.1
body:
## @oh-my-pi/pi-agent-core

### Added

- Added `Agent.peekDeliveringMessages(queue?)` for queued input on its way into the next request that the transcript has not recorded yet; queue listeners hear when it lands.
- Added `Agent.continue(signal, { queuedOnly: true })` to start an idle turn using queued input without making a separate model call for the current context.

### Changed

- Debug logs now time the wait between dequeuing input and the model request that carries it, by phase.

## @oh-my-pi/pi-ai

### Added

- Fast-tier requests now prefer eligible credentials, including Codex plans with Ultrafast, Claude accounts with fast mode, and stored or environment API keys. Eligible accounts continue serving on paid overage and within their reserve, while normal load balancing resumes when the requested tier is unavailable or refused.

### Changed

- Embeddings, transcription, and video errors now present upstream error messages clearly when available instead of exposing raw JSON response bodies.

### Fixed

- Fixed Codex requests incorrectly sending a service tier to accounts whose plans do not support it.
- Successful OAuth token refreshes now restore normal account selection after a temporary refresh outage.

## @oh-my-pi/pi-catalog

### Fixed

- Fixed Codex service tiers, such as Ultrafast, being hidden for accounts that support them when the first logged-in account has a plan that does not.

## @oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent

### Breaking Changes

- Removed several internal utility exports from the coding-agent package. Import `errorMessage` from `@oh-my-pi/pi-utils/type-guards`, `flattenLine` from `@oh-my-pi/pi-tui/text/sanitize`, and `fuzzyHits` from `@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent/utils/fuzzy`; import `stripInlineMarkdown` from `plan-mode/plan-toc`.

### Added

- Background processes started by the bash tool are now detected when the agent stops, allowing them to be registered as services or terminated; background jobs using `&` are cleaned up when the session ends. Configure this behavior with `bash.reapBackground` (RPC mode does not reap processes).
- Added the `o2ctl services` shell commands for adopting an existing process as a named service, listing services, and stopping services.
- Agents can change their own model or a live child agent's model through the `agent://<id>/model` interface, including permitted user-tagged models, and adjust reasoning effort through `agent://<id>/effort` or a model suffix.
- In Tern, pasted-image attachments can be opened in the image annotator; completing annotation replaces the attachment with the edited image.
- Added `archive.transcript(id, { detail, budget, turns })` for rendering compacted, budget-limited views of previous evaluation sessions, with controls for transcript detail and turn ranges.

### Changed

- Session identifiers and session-file paths are now available to all commands run within a session, including evaluation shell commands, `!` commands, `/loop` conditions, and autoresearch runs.
- Isolated subagent and `/wt` ovnfs checkouts now record the session that created or moved into them, and `ovnfs ls` displays that session after the supporting daemon is restarted.
- `/fast` and `/fast ultra` automatically select an eligible account or stored API key, fall back to other accounts at standard speed when limits are reached, and resume using the fast account when it recovers. Refused fast-mode requests no longer disable `/fast` when another eligible credential remains available.
- `history://<id>` now uses the enhanced transcript view with numbered turns, grouped consecutive reads and searches, and `budget`, `detail`, and `turns` query parameters.
- Tern's agent tray now shows running and queued agents before completed agents, with each group ordered by spawn time.

### Fixed

- A queued or steered message keeps its queue pill until it appears in the transcript, instead of vanishing while its request is still being prepared.
- Fixed LSP diagnostics failing to load when imported before the LSP tool.
- Model lookups now reflect catalog changes from an extension provider’s OAuth login, including in mirrored registries.
- Tern browser actions now report the last observed reason a target was not actionable and discard target coordinates received after the deadline.
- Fixed checkout and workspace detection for paths inside directories whose names begin with `..`, so scoped settings, plugin roots, and folder restrictions apply correctly.
- Fixed broadcasts arriving while a subagent is finishing so they no longer replace the subagent's final report.
- On Linux, bash `time -l` and `time -v` now report the measured program's peak memory usage rather than the agent process's usage.
- Fixed zsh scripts rendered in the pseudo shell so shell syntax is displayed correctly instead of replacement characters.
- Fixed ACP session loading and resuming for saved Copilot 1M models during background model-catalog refreshes.
- Fixed Tern browser actions that ran out of time mid-wait reporting a transport timeout instead of why the element was not actionable (disabled, covered, moving).
- Fixed extension OAuth catalog modifiers (`oauth.modifyModels`) not rerunning on a model-catalog refresh when `models.yml` is unchanged or missing, so a login no longer leaves other providers' models unmodified until restart.
- Fixed `tui.colorfulMarkdown: false` and `tui.renderMermaid: false` so they apply consistently to assistant replies, thinking, user prompts, extension messages, summaries, and tool output.
- Fixed rules supplied by extensions in configuration overlays from disappearing when the system prompt is rebuilt.
- Fixed idle follow-ups becoming stuck after extension messages or compaction summaries.
- Fixed resuming goals whose token budget is exhausted so they remain budget-limited, and prevented incomplete-goal reminders from asking the agent to continue while budget-limited.
- Assistant replies show SVG fences and HTML image and page embeds inline again on terminals that support graphics ([#20508](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/issues/20508)).

## @oh-my-pi/pi-natives

### Added

- Added `Shell.heldProcesses()` to inspect all live external processes held by a shell session, including background and `nohup` jobs, with their `nohup` status.
- Added process utilities for finding processes by inherited environment variables, inspecting process details and output files, and terminating process families while preserving `nohup` processes when requested.
- Added an in-process Perl 5.34 shell builtin with core language and regex support, common command-line options and modules, and shell-integrated file and command I/O, including support for `scheme://` paths and other shell builtins.

### Fixed

- Fixed timed-out, cancelled, or terminated shell and PTY commands leaving descendant processes running, including descendants in separate process groups or sessions.
- Fixed cancelled filesystem searches continuing in the background and consuming CPU or blocking subsequent filesystem operations when multiple searches ran concurrently.

## @oh-my-pi/pi-tui

### Breaking Changes

- Removed the public `oneLine` export from `@oh-my-pi/pi-tui/term/painters/picker`; use `flattenLine` from `@oh-my-pi/pi-tui/text/sanitize` instead.

### Added

- Added the `change` UI event for annotated images, delivered to the node’s `onChange` handler without an associated item.

### Fixed

- Panes in a background Tern tab no longer log frame-acknowledgment stall warnings.

## @oh-my-pi/pi-utils

### Added

- Added path utilities for checking whether a path exists and whether it is lexically contained within another path without resolving symlinks.
- Added `errorMessage()` to `@oh-my-pi/pi-utils/type-guards` for retrieving message text from thrown values.
- Added `Laps` for timing the phases of a multi-step async path as one log record.

### Fixed

- Fixed path containment checks for files and directories whose names begin with `..`.

## @oh-my-pi/pi-wire

### Added

- Added the TSP `annotate` image action, including its `change` event for delivering the annotated picture.
- Added shared collab link support for generating, formatting, parsing, and normalizing relay-based collaboration links.


## What's Changed
* fix(tui): applied the markdown look setting to every markdown surface by @roboomp in https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/20474
* fix(sdk): kept overlay extension rules across prompt rebuilds by @roboomp in https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/20476
* fix(goal): kept spent goals budget-limited across resume by @roboomp in https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/20457
* refactor(coding-agent): remove ExtensionUiController.initializeHookRunner by @H4vC in https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/20494
* refactor(utils): add pathExists and fold three identical copies by @H4vC in https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/20483
* refactor(coding-agent): keep one agent-hub formatCost by @H4vC in https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/20487
* refactor(coding-agent): share the metacpan resource and dependency sections by @H4vC in https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/20488
* refactor(ai): one request skeleton for the embeddings, rerank and transcriptions gateway routes by @H4vC in https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/20492
* refactor(tui): share Emitter and MemoryStdin between the testing terminal doubles by @H4vC in https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/20495
* refactor(coding-agent): share /todo parsing helpers between the TUI controller and the slash handler by @H4vC in https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/20486
* refactor: fold equivalent local record guards into pi-utils isRecord/asRecord by @H4vC in https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/20480
* refactor(wire): share the collab link codec between host and web client by @H4vC in https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/20489
* refactor(ai): parse endpoint error bodies through OpenAIHttpError.parseEnvelope by @H4vC in https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/20490
* refactor(ai): share the bounded request body reader across endpoint servers by @H4vC in https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/20491
* refactor(coding-agent): merge discovery load results through one helper by @H4vC in https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/20493
* refactor(utils): add pathIsWithinLexical and fold six local copies by @H4vC in https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/20481
* fix(utils): treat ..name children as inside the root in path containment by @H4vC in https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/20482
* refactor(utils): fold local errorMessage copies into pi-utils by @H4vC in https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/20479
* refactor(coding-agent): fold flattenLine and displayLines copies into pi-tui text/sanitize by @H4vC in https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/20484
* refactor(coding-agent): remove three duplicated helper bodies by @H4vC in https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/20485

name: v3.24.5 — A citation re-check after revision, an exact-title Tier 0 rule, and a premise check for a claim the user names
body:
> **Citation, source-verification, and formatter repairs and one new step the user asks for; no new skill or mode, and the prompt-level changes are unmeasured:** In `academic-paper` `full` mode, citations are re-checked before Phase 7 when a Phase 6 revision round or the Option A edit added, removed, or changed a citation or a reference-list entry, and the formatter uses the re-check's draft and reference list (#1071). A citation edit the user asks for in chat outside a revision round is not covered; it is tracked in #1145. The formatter keeps a citation or a reference-list entry that a reported incoming mismatch requires it to keep, and a preserved entry still has to follow the target format; the CHANGELOG entries give the exact exceptions (#1152, #1155, #1161). These citation and formatter rules are prompt-level. The Tier 0 prompt accepts a title-search or DOI match only on an exact normalized title and also requires the first author's family name to match (#1146). The author check, and the exact-title check on a DOI hit, are prompt-level; the scripts were not changed for these checks. The OpenAlex, Crossref, and arXiv protocols now describe the same exact-title rule for title search (#1148). Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, and Crossref DOI lookups and arXiv ID lookups reject a hit when either title normalizes to an empty string (#1163, #1166). A Crossref retraction and reinstatement for the cited DOI with the same latest timestamp now give `disputed` in either input order (#1150). A Crossref retraction and reinstatement whose dates are too imprecise to order give `disputed`, and a year-only or year-month notice date is no longer reported as an exact notice date (#1154, #1170). OpenAlex, Crossref, and arXiv raise their unavailable errors when a request fails before a status line arrives or the status line is invalid, and Semantic Scholar stops sending requests for the batch after a malformed status line (#1181). OpenAlex, Crossref, and arXiv also skip a title search when the reference title is null or normalizes to empty (#1171, #1177, #1180). In the formatter, a word-count deviation of 1% or more triggers a section-by-section comparison and no longer fails the check by itself (#1162). The formatter puts Vancouver in-text numbers in parentheses and IEEE numbers in square brackets; only in the blind-review version do the integrity checks allow the removal of all author information, as the Author Information step directs; and when the input author list is already truncated and the required names are unavailable, the formatter adds no names and raises the missing names as a content issue (#1172). These formatter rules are prompt-level. When the user asks to check a claim's premises, `source_verification_agent` lists one to four premises and marks each against the sources that passed Reference Existence Verification; it never accepts or rejects the claim, and it is a prompt-level, single-agent assessment (#1128, #1133). A claim with more than four conditions can be split incompletely with no mark that the split is partial, and when no premise is marked as needed, the `Reading` can say that every needed premise holds even though no premise has support; the unsupported premises are still flagged, and the claim as a whole still gets the two-independent-source cross-check. Smaller repairs: the Phase 6 review inputs name the draft each round reviews (#1136), the Phase 6a lint instructions allow the #684 pointer authority (#1143), two committee-correspondence pointers now match the Activation gate (#1123, #1132), `timeline_extraction_agent` no longer cites a check that does not exist (#1129), after a resume or a compaction the SessionStart announce uses the plugin agents' current names (#1168), and the arXiv protocol says that a citation with no arXiv ID skips the arXiv resolver (#1178). The README names the DeepSeek Harness (DSH) sibling distribution, which does not port the Claude Code hooks and whose code the ARS maintainer did not audit or run (#1126), and three translated READMEs add the `rebuttal-audit` example (#1176).

### Added

- **The README names the DeepSeek Harness (DSH) sibling distribution maintained by TY-Cheng (#1126).** It is recognized under the platform-ports policy in `CONTRIBUTING.md`. The ARS maintainer verified that its vendored skill and core files match the pinned upstream commit and reviewed its README and submission documents; the ARS maintainer did not audit the port's code or run it. The README entry states the port's limits. The Claude Code hooks are not ported. Its documented run used version 0.3.0 of the port, before its native DSH team skills and tools, ran all role prompts inline in one session, and used a model that its agent reported as `deepseek-flash`. That run shows no separate user decision at the review or Stage 5 entry checkpoints, and it predates the checkpoint rules that version 0.4.5 added to the port's `ars-pipeline-team` skill.

- **`source_verification_agent` can split a claim into premises when the user explicitly asks to check that claim's premises (#1128, #1133, contributed by @SID-6921).** It lists one to four premises, marks each `HOLDS`, `UNSUPPORTED`, or `CONTRADICTED` against the sources that passed Reference Existence Verification, and marks which premises the claim needs. It reports what follows and never accepts or rejects the claim; the claim as a whole still gets the two-independent-source cross-check. A list of claims in `fact-check` mode does not trigger it. It is a single-agent assessment. A follow-up maintainer edit made the trigger wording in Boundaries, the `Reading` cases, which the needed premises alone now decide, and the `fact-check` case agree. A claim with more than four conditions can exceed the premise limit, and the pass does not mark such a split as partial. When no premise is marked as needed, for example when a claim of the form "A or B" is split into two alternatives, the `Reading` can say that every needed premise holds even though no premise has support; the flags for the unsupported premises and the cross-check still follow. Prompt-level; unmeasured.

- **The Traditional Chinese, Simplified Chinese, and Japanese READMEs list the `rebuttal-audit` usage example (#1176, contributed by @yhsindev).** The Japanese line keeps the English request text, as the English README has it.

### Fixed

- **Literature resolvers now treat dropped connections and malformed HTTP status lines as API failures (#1181, contributed by @pinjun99).** OpenAlex, Crossref, and arXiv raise their existing unavailable errors when a request fails before a status line arrives or the status line is invalid. Semantic Scholar also latches the outage on a malformed status line and skips further requests for the batch.

- **The `academic-paper` formatter uses parentheses for Vancouver in-text numbers and square brackets for IEEE (#1172, #1186, contributed by @pinjun99).** A word-count deviation of 1% or more triggers a section-by-section comparison. In the blind-review version only, the integrity checks allow removal of all author information as directed by the Author Information step, and recovery leaves it out. Other missing content is restored. The conversion checklist preserves the spelling of in-text author names where shown and checks reference-list names against the target style and applicable journal requirements. When the input list is already truncated and required names are unavailable, it adds no names and raises the missing names as a content issue. Prompt-level change, unmeasured.

- **A resolved Crossref notice date is published only when the latest occurrence is known to the day, and conflicting dates for one notice stay `disputed` when they can change the winner (#1170, contributed by @pinjun99).** For a year-only or year-month Crossref notice, `event_date` and `retraction_event_date` no longer report 1 January or the first of that month as an exact notice date. An acquisition date inside the possible range, including either endpoint, gives `not_decidable`. An acquisition date strictly before the range gives `after_acquisition`. An acquisition date strictly after the range gives `before_acquisition`. When the notice day is established, acquisition on that day gives `same_day`. `event_date` is null for a lone `[2024]` or `[2024, 2]`, and for distinct same-kind notices at `[2024]` and `[2024, 2, 10]`; the verdict is still `retracted` or `reinstated`. When `date-parts` gives only a year or a year and month, that precision is kept even if a `date-time` is also present. A three-part `date-parts` date still prefers a valid `date-time`, including its time of day. Usable `date-parts` still apply when the timestamp is invalid, and a usable timestamp still applies when `date-parts` are absent or malformed. One retraction DOI dated 10 February 2024 and 10 October 2024, with a reinstatement on 1 June 2024, yields `disputed` rather than `retracted`, including when the two retraction reports arrive through `updated-by` and `update-to`. Two different retraction DOIs on those dates still yield `retracted`, and a reinstatement after every possible date of the earlier notice still wins. With no opposite-kind notice, those two dates for one retraction DOI stay `retracted` and `event_date` is null. A year and a day reported for the same notice still cover the whole year.

- **The `academic-paper` formatter's content-integrity check uses the word count only as a trigger (#1162, contributed by @TanmayShah29).** In the Quality Gates row and the Pre-Output Final Checklist item of `academic-paper/agents/formatter_agent.md`, a word-count deviation of 1% or more triggers a section-by-section comparison with the Draft, the selected reference list, and the bilingual abstracts and keywords. A deviation alone no longer fails the check; any lost content does, and so does text the conversion duplicated and text it added that is in none of those inputs. A section `formatter_agent.md` tells the formatter to add, such as the Data Availability Statement or the AI Disclosure Statement, may be added once when the Draft does not already have it; a second copy still fails, and a missing Abstract or Limitations section is still reported, not written. An incomplete AI Disclosure Statement may be completed in place with the standard text, and the AI Disclosure row's Failure Handling says so. A word-count change from converting the citation style, in either direction, or from reformatting reference-list entries to the target style is neither lost nor added content. The Quality Gates row now also carries the #548 protected-hedges exception. The Failure Handling cell and the Failure Handling Strategies tree remove only text the conversion duplicated and additions the check does not allow, so an incoming duplicate reference-list entry kept in `full` mode (#1071) stays. `tests/test_formatter_1162.py` pins the wording of the row, both checklist items, the repair branch and the AI Disclosure repair cell, including the compared quantity. Prompt-level; unmeasured.

- **The OpenAlex, Crossref, and arXiv protocols now describe the exact-title search rule from #431 (#1148, contributed by @pinjun99).** All three protocols require an exact normalized title for title search and describe the matching-year preference among exact candidates. The DOI and arXiv ID cross-checks identify `_similarity` as the title score and retain the 0.70 threshold. `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` now gives the S2 Tier 0 title and first-author requirements. The existing prompt-sync test covers the three protocols and both architecture rows. Prompt-level; unmeasured.

- **The arXiv protocol and the `arxiv_unmatched` schema description now say that the arXiv resolver skips a citation with no arXiv ID (#1178, #1182, contributed by @Golden007-prog).** One arXiv-specific note in the protocol had said that such a citation is checked by title search only. The revised note says to skip the arXiv resolver and omit `arxiv_unmatched` when the citation has no arXiv ID, and to use title search only when the ID lookup returns no entry or fails the title cross-check. The schema description now says that the check runs only for non-manual entries with an arXiv ID. Documentation only.

- **After a resume or a compaction, the SessionStart announce names the plugin agents by their #1037 names (#1168, contributed by @AyhamJo7).** The `compact|resume` branch of `scripts/announce-ars-loaded.sh` still listed `synthesis_agent`, `research_architect_agent`, `report_compiler_agent`, and `screening_reviewer_agent`; it now lists `synthesis-agent`, `research-architect-agent`, `report-compiler-agent`, and `screening-reviewer-agent`, as the startup branch does. A test in `scripts/test_check_command_skill_dispatch.py` runs the hook for `startup`, `clear`, `resume`, `compact`, and `fork` and checks that the context has one `Plugin agents` list and that it matches the frontmatter `name` of each file in `agents/`.

- **Identifier matches now require text in both normalized titles (#1163, #1166, contributed by @pinjun99).** Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, and Crossref DOI lookups and arXiv ID lookups reject hits when either title normalizes to an empty string. Semantic Scholar also skips title search when the reference title normalizes to an empty string.

- **OpenAlex, Crossref, and arXiv now skip title searches when the reference title is null or normalizes to empty, and handle null reference titles during identifier cross-checks (#1171, #1177, #1180, contributed by @pinjun99).** Crossref treats a null first title variant as missing. Semantic Scholar title search skips hits without a paper ID so a later valid hit can match.

- **Crossref retraction and reinstatement notices now yield `disputed` when their reported dates are too imprecise to order (#1154, contributed by @pinjun99).** Notices in different years, or in different months when both specify a month, can still be ordered. A retraction reported as both 2024 and 10 February 2024 remains disputed against a 1 June 2024 reinstatement. Reports of one notice at more than one precision still cover the coarser date (#1170).

- **Conflicting Crossref notices with the same latest timestamp now yield `disputed` (#1150, contributed by @pinjun99).** When a retraction and a reinstatement for the cited DOI share the latest timestamp, either input order produces the same verdict.

- **`academic-paper` `full` mode Phase 6 review inputs name the Phase 5a Corrected Draft for the first review and the writer's Revised Draft with its Revision Log for later rounds (#1136, contributed by @flipcyde101).** `academic-paper/SKILL.md` (Phase 6a overview and Phase 6b user content) and `academic-paper/agents/peer_reviewer_agent.md` (Complete Review Workflow input and Phase 6a/6b contract prompts) previously named the Phase 4b draft (or Complete Draft), contradicting `peer_reviewer_agent.md`'s Input Sources table after #1068. Prompt-level; unmeasured.

- **`commands/ars-revision-coach.md` names the Activation gate in `committee_correspondence_protocol.md` as the place that decides which comments the committee-correspondence variant covers (#1123, #1132, contributed by @SID-6921).** The scope-pointer test in `scripts/test_check_committee_correspondence.py` now checks this file too.

- **The `academic-paper` mode guide's committee branch names resubmission organization, as the Activation gate does (#1123 point 5, contributed by @TanmayShah29).** A new test in `scripts/test_check_committee_correspondence.py` checks that the decision tree's committee line and the gate list the same three requests.

- **`timeline_extraction_agent` no longer cites a v3.9.4 extension of `scripts/check_pipeline_integrity.py` that does not exist (#1129, reported by @SID-6921).** Its enforcement sentence now names the advisory verifier as the other Bucket A agents do, and `CANONICAL_ENFORCEMENT["4"]` in `scripts/check_v3_9_2_phase_boundary.py` carries the same sentence. The verifier and the write-scope guard are unchanged.

- **`academic-paper` full mode re-checks citations before Phase 7 (#1071, contributed by @pinjun99).** The re-check runs if any Phase 6 revision round or the Option A edit added, removed, or changed a citation or a reference-list entry. The formatter uses the re-check's Corrected Draft and its reference list. The Phase 5a report is kept alongside the re-check report, with its correction log when Phase 5a produced one. The re-check verifies sources as usual and records conflicts in Items Flagged for Review. The reviewer gives Final Counts with every Accept. The formatter skips confirmation and uses those counts only when the Phase 7 draft and its reference list both match the accepted draft and its `## References` section; the caller makes that comparison. If the re-check changed a citation or a reference-list entry after acceptance, the formatter shows `Citations changed after Round N acceptance; this version has not been re-reviewed`, asks once, and counts the draft itself. Before conversion, it compares the draft and list using the selected style's rules for which works require an entry and which entries require a citation. Missing, uncited, or duplicate entries appear in an Output Package warning. Formatting continues with citation content preserved. A citation edit the user asks for in chat outside a revision round is not covered and is tracked in #1145. Prompt-level only. The effect on runs is unmeasured.

- **The `academic-paper` full-mode Phase 6a evaluator prompt now allows the paper-blind #684 pointer authority in its lint instructions (#1143, contributed by @pinjun99).** This agrees with the instruction to reproduce the supplied `INTERNAL` binding marker after the Scoring Plan. Prompt-level; unmeasured.

- **Tier 0 title search follows the resolvers' exact-title rule from #431, and the prompt also requires an exact title on DOI hits (#1146, contributed by @pinjun99).** The prompt text still accepted a match at title similarity >= 0.70 with a year match, so a cited work whose title is close to a different paper ("Attention Is All You Need" against "Attention Is Not All You Need", 0.926) could become `S2_VERIFIED` and skip the Tier 2 spot-check. A title-search candidate now passes the title check only when the two titles are equal under any of the three forms in `exact_normalized_title` (`scripts/_text_similarity.py`). `S2_VERIFIED` also needs the first author's family name, compared case-insensitively, and the check fails if either side has no author; a generic title such as `Editorial` cannot pass by title search. A DOI candidate needs the same two checks. The first-author check, and exact-title verification on a DOI candidate, are prompt-level: the scripts do not compare authors, and `_lookup_by_doi` returns `matched: True` once the DOI title cross-check clears its 0.70 threshold. Year is not a Tier 0 pass condition. The prompt uses matching year only as a tie-break among title-search candidates that pass both checks. The resolver's title-search scoring adds 0.05 when the year is equal among candidates that already have an exact normalized title and does not compare authors. The title score is `_similarity` in `scripts/_text_similarity.py`: it returns 1.0 for a Chinese-aware exact match and otherwise takes the higher of the base and dotted-acronym `difflib.SequenceMatcher.ratio()` scores, not a Levenshtein distance. Title search has required an exact normalized title since #431, and the helper now accepts the three forms. Only the `DOI_MISMATCH` threshold stayed at 0.70. A DOI candidate below 0.70 is `DOI_MISMATCH`. A DOI candidate at or above 0.70 whose title is not an exact normalized match is neither `DOI_MISMATCH` nor `S2_VERIFIED` and goes on to Tier 1 and Tier 2. The scripts are unchanged. Prompt-level; unmeasured.

- **The `academic-paper` formatter's two #1071 quality-gate exceptions now apply only to an item that a reported incoming mismatch requires it to keep (#1152, reported by @Imbad0202).** In the `Format compliance` and `Journal requirements` rows, the sentence from #1127 could be read as letting any citation left verbatim pass, including one the formatter failed to convert; the condition now comes first and covers both the retained citation and the preserved reference-list entry. The earlier wording came from the maintainer's review of #1127. Prompt-level; unmeasured.

- **A reference-list entry that the `academic-paper` formatter preserves for a reported incoming mismatch still has to follow the target format (#1161, reported by @Imbad0202).** In `full` mode, the Step 4 format compliance check and the `Format compliance` quality gate let such an entry pass the whole check, so a preserved entry with a missing number or a wrong format passed. Now a citation retained verbatim still passes, and a preserved entry is exempt only from a rule that would remove it. In the `Journal requirements` row, the exception now covers only the affected citation or entry: a requirement that would change a retained citation or remove a preserved entry does not apply to it, the Output Package warning names that requirement, and every other citation and entry is checked as usual. The earlier wording came from #1152 and #1156. Prompt-level; unmeasured.

- **The `academic-paper` formatter's Step 4 format compliance check now accepts a reference-list entry that a reported incoming mismatch requires it to preserve in `full` mode (#1155, contributed by @pinjun99).** Step 4 now applies the same exception as the Format compliance quality gate to both that entry and a citation the mismatch requires retaining verbatim. Prompt-level; unmeasured.

name: openclaw 2026.10.34
body:
This is a gateway-only `extended-stable` release, which is our current equivalent to LTS. This release is OpenClaw from the end of October 2026, plus critical security updates, reliability and performance fixes, and features like new model support. The latest version of OpenClaw at the time of this release is [2026.11.10](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases#release-v2026.11.10)

## 2026.10.34

This extended-stable patch updates the Gateway and official npm plugins from 2026.10.33. It includes the core npm package and Gateway Docker images, but no native-app releases.

### Highlights

- OpenAI and ClawRouter: select GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, with system-prompt caching on the OpenAI API-key and Sign in with ChatGPT Responses routes. (#200766, #201094) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @RomneyDa, @fuller-stack-dev, and @obviyus.
- Tlon: group DMs use their own approval policy, and approved clubs remain authorized across Gateway restarts. (#202775) Thanks @joshavant.
- Update recovery: avoid leaving the Gateway offline when an update runs alongside database readers or replaces a running checkout, and recover the service after a failed Windows update rolls back. (#201330, #202541, #203241, #203264) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @RomneyDa.
- Conversation continuity: deliver ready child results without waiting for other helpers to finish, and accept follow-up chat messages after the preceding run completes. (#203176, #203102, #201790) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @obviyus, @RomneyDa, and @vincentkoc.
- Channel delivery: recover Telegram polling when update IDs reset, keep an undownloadable attachment from blocking replies, and reconnect all Discord accounts after a network outage. (#201167, #200682, #201415, #162189) Thanks @RomneyDa, @obviyus, and @mattreyes0824.

### Changes

- MiniMax: stop offering retired M2 models, including during live discovery, and use MiniMax-M3 for PDF text extraction. If your configuration explicitly selects an M2 model, switch it to a supported model. (#203998) Thanks @RomneyDa.

### Fixes

- Access controls: apply the session permission mode consistently on Gateway tool calls, recheck bound Discord DMs against current policy, and keep Signal view-once attachments out of assistant context. (#202941, #196848, #196841) Thanks @obviyus and @drobison00.
- Channel setup: save new tokens through the channel secret store rather than writing them to config as plaintext. (#201428, #175333) Thanks @anmol0b, @sallyom, and @masatohoshino.
- Discord and Slack: queue independent Discord requests instead of replacing an active task, show when the target session is busy, and leave Slack question buttons available when a click comes from someone who cannot answer. (#201518, #201363, #201371, #201348) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @vincentkoc, @obviyus, and @shannon0430.
- Conversation delivery: return complete queued ACP replies, preserve Claude CLI final answers after progress messages, and avoid repeating tool work on a fallback model during long Claude CLI turns. (#202658, #200470, #200801, #200744) Thanks @obviyus, @chaeyn, @fede-kamel, and @jzmudzinski.
- Conversation recovery: resume saved requests when transcript metadata advances, and keep pending child results when the requesting run ends or a follow-up takes over. (#201477, #195275) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @RomneyDa and @jalehman.
- OpenAI and Codex: preserve session affinity for Sign in with ChatGPT and let Codex subagents start from agent folders with capital letters. (#197588, #197532, #201520, #201423) Thanks @sukhdeepjohar, @aatreya, @obviyus, and @thejeys19.
- Provider reliability: compact before predicted context overflow instead of trimming tool results already cached by the provider, stop retrying Anthropic requests that require credits, and preserve user-configured model rows on provider sign-in. (#199530, #201997, #201742, #201558) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @obviyus, @LinzeShi, @MertBasar0, and @Caitoz.
- Install and update: avoid hanging at NodeSource on Ubuntu 26.04, preserve pnpm-linked checkouts when switching to the npm release, and complete updates with read-only, unchanged config or old plugin leases. (#203538, #201701, #201331, #201314) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @fuller-stack-dev.
- Storage and backups: let large PostgreSQL maintenance operations finish, recover after silent database connection loss, port upgraded stores to PostgreSQL, and reclaim space when backup staging databases are deleted. (#201869, #201856, #201299, #201250, #199666) Thanks @VACInc, @chelsealong, @evemorgen, and @etzelm.
- Doctor: reuse the existing state database for offline update checks after backup, avoiding extra copies of large databases. (#202985) Authored by @steipete.
- Browser and Control UI: capture background tabs in headed or headless Chrome, keep final answers out of the collapsed Worked fold, and preserve pending dictation transcripts while showing progress. (#202878, #165312, #201626, #197429, #200235) Thanks @obviyus, @titan550, @Marvinthebored, @vyctorbrzezowski, @Peetiegonzalez, and @daniel-lxs.
- Automation and Feishu: deliver automation failure notices back to the chat that created the job and finish long replies in the same streaming card. (#203056, #161777, #139443) Thanks @obviyus, @ArthurNie, and @Simon2256928.

This audited record covers the complete v2026.10.33..3656180a44de203e4b3be5fb02d768fcdb306767 history: 129 in-range PRs + 0 retained seed-only PRs = 129 unique PRs. The generation manifest also supplies direct commits as editorial input; the grouped notes above prioritize user impact.

name: v2.4.2
body:
### Highlights

- **GPT-6.2 System Prompt**: GPT-6.2 Sol and Astra, and the `gpt-latest` aliases, use a system prompt written for GPT-6.2. ([#66297](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/66297))
- **OpenCode Go Onboarding Fix**: After you connect OpenCode, the model picker lists OpenCode Go first. ([#66363](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/66363))
- **Esc Takes Back Your Last Message**: If the composer is empty, stopping a response with Esc before the model has written anything or called a tool removes your message and puts it back in the composer, images included, so you can edit it and send again. ([#65505](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/65505))

### Upgrade notes

- **"Always allow" for a web fetch allows that site only.** It used to allow every URL. Approvals saved by earlier versions stay as they were. ([#66000](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/66000))
- **Automations keep running after a failed run.** A failed run is recorded and the next one runs on schedule. Automations still pause when the session that created them or their directory is gone, or when their setup is no longer valid. A shell command in an automation's code that runs past its timeout is now stopped and fails the call instead of moving to the background. ([#66422](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/66422), [#65626](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/65626))
- **Sending to an archived session unarchives it.** This applies to messages, commands, skills and shell commands, including ones sent through the API. ([#66348](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/66348))
- **Plan mode's rules are in the system prompt.** Sessions already in Plan mode get the rules once more after upgrading. ([#63669](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63669))

### Core

#### Improvements

- Added a system prompt for GPT-6.2. ([#66297](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/66297))
- `generate_image` and `generate_video` run inside Code Mode instead of as top-level tools, so their definitions no longer add about 700 tokens to every request. ([#66465](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/66465))
- Moving a session also moves its subagents. ([#66215](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/66215))
- The `report` skill checks the docs, searches for duplicate issues and includes the relevant log lines. ([#66290](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/66290))
- Cost estimates for service tiers that list their own prices use those prices, including their long-context rates. ([#65861](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/65861), [#65984](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/65984))

#### Bug fixes

- Fixed sign-in to MCP servers whose configured URL has a query string, such as the AWS MCP Server. ([#66036](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/66036))
- Fixed Plan mode re-adding its reminder after every compaction, which could keep a session running in a loop. ([#63669](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63669))
- Fixed tools staying visible to the model when a blanket deny was followed by narrower denies. ([#65899](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/65899))
- Fixed PDFs with bytes before the `%PDF-` header not being read as PDFs. ([#65967](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/65967))
- Fixed branches whose names end in `/HEAD` missing from the branch list. ([#65904](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/65904))
- Fixed files added by a patch losing a trailing blank line. ([#66378](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/66378))
- Fixed moving a session to a `~\` path on Windows. ([#66269](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/66269))
- Fixed OpenAI custom tool calls failing as malformed on providers that end them only with the completed response. ([#65849](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/65849))

### TUI

#### Improvements

- The model picker stays responsive with large catalogs, such as OpenRouter's. ([#66370](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/66370))
- The goal dialog scrolls when the goal is long. ([#65906](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/65906))
- Updated OpenTUI to 0.9.9. ([#65919](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/65919))

#### Bug fixes

- Fixed `/models` showing only free models when the TUI opened a session in another directory. ([#66424](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/66424))
- Fixed type-to-filter in Message Actions. ([#65903](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/65903))
- Fixed removing `theme` from config not switching back to the default theme. ([#65925](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/65925))
- Fixed quick successive settings changes overwriting each other. ([#65761](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/65761))
- Fixed the session list losing the selected row after a deletion. ([#65855](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/65855))

### Desktop

#### Improvements

- On macOS and Windows, desktop updates download only the parts of the app that changed instead of the full installer again. ([#66042](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/66042))
- Enter in the question dock moves to the next question and submits on the last one. Set **Submit question answers with** to Cmd/Ctrl+Enter in **Settings → Preferences** to keep the previous behavior. ([#66169](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/66169))
- To move the file tree to the right in the Files and Review panels, right-click its header and choose **Sidebar position → Right**. ([#66012](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/66012))
- `/rename` with no title generates a new title, and `/rename <title>` sets one. ([#66396](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/66396))
- Search sessions also finds archived sessions and shows them dimmed. ([#66356](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/66356))
- In the Inbox sidebar, you can pin sessions, open archived sessions in a collapsible section and choose where working sessions appear. Archived sessions waiting on you show under Needs attention. ([#65961](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/65961), [#66327](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/66327))
- Cmd+Shift+S (Ctrl+Shift+S on Windows and Linux) unarchives the open session when it's archived. ([#66327](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/66327))

name: v0.45.0
body:
### New Features

- Added a **Firefox engine** driven over WebDriver BiDi: pass `--engine firefox` (or set `AGENT_BROWSER_ENGINE=firefox`) with Firefox 150 or newer to drive a local Firefox install with snapshots and `@eN` refs across open and closed shadow roots and iframes, `find` locators, shared form preconditions and error codes (`fill`, `type`, `check`, `uncheck`, `select --by`), right-click, middle-click, and modifier keys (`--button`, `--modifiers`), network routes and HAR capture, `--allowed-domains`, downloads, viewport, media, geolocation, header, and offline emulation, isolated windows, `--pin-tab`, screenshots, PDF export, and dashboard live view (#2205, #2206, #2207, #2208, #2595, #2633)
- Added **Firefox attach mode**: connect to an existing Firefox instance over WebDriver BiDi with `--cdp` or `connect` (including `ws://.../session?devtools=<port>` endpoints), apply live settings in place, and detach on `close` without closing the running browser (#2227)

### Bug Fixes

- Fixed **keyboard `keydown`, `keyup`, and `press` modifier handling**: `keydown` and `keyup` now send `code`, `keyCode`, `location`, and printable text and carry held modifiers across subsequent keyboard, mouse, and flow-recorder commands. `press` applies US-layout Shift mapping, suppresses printable text for Alt, Control, and Meta chords, and dispatches modifier key events for chords not already held (#2734)
- Fixed **saved flow host rules, write consent, deadlines, and result shaping**: saved host rules now match hostnames regardless of case or a trailing DNS root dot, non-`POST` requests carrying GraphQL queries require write declarations and consent, HTTP preflight cookie and route lookups and in-page fetches stop at the run deadline, empty result lists no longer fail `--fields` or `--where`, and `--limit` shapes only retained rows (#2735)
- Fixed **saved flow replay** finishing before late-reported first-party Chrome requests settle (#2711)
- Fixed **iframe targeting**: `frame` resolves cross-origin, unnamed, and nested iframes by CSS selector or `@ref`, and selector commands, `find` locators, `wait`, `check`, and `uncheck` act inside the selected frame, including same-site cross-origin iframes, without reaching tabs pinned by other sessions (#2737)
- Fixed **`eval` and `console` in iframes**: `eval` runs in the frame selected with `frame` and reports that frame's origin, and `console` and `errors` capture messages from cross-origin iframes on the active tab (#2738)
- Fixed **iframe snapshots and annotated screenshots**: snapshots label iframes by their `title` or `name`, and `screenshot --annotate` places boxes for elements inside iframes in page coordinates, including cross-origin, scrolled, and scaled frames (#2739)
- Fixed **dashboard live view pointer and tabs**: clicks map to the real page size, drags send held buttons, touchpad two-finger taps open the context menu, and a tab that closes itself resyncs the tab bar (#2744)
- Fixed **dashboard live view keyboard and clipboard**: editing shortcuts such as select all, undo, and line navigation reach the page, Option and AltGr characters type, and copy, cut, and paste work through the live view without granting the browser clipboard permissions (#2745)
- Fixed **`state save` collection**: it no longer stalls under `--allowed-domains`, sends requests to previously visited origins, runs their service workers, or brings a temporary tab to the front. It includes origins from attached sessions but not tabs pinned by other sessions, and keeps the previous autosave when collection fails (#2746)
- Fixed **`state list`, `state show`, and bulk storage reads**: `state list` shows modified dates, `state show` reports cookie and origin counts (`cookieCount` and `originCount` in JSON, with `summary` unchanged), and `storage local` and `storage session` keep keys such as `__proto__` (#2747)

### Documentation

- Added the **Firefox engine guide** (`/engines/firefox`) and updated CLI help, MCP tool schemas, command references, and core skills for Firefox support and form command behavior (#2208, #2227, #2595, #2633)

name: v16.2.1
body: - **After a release ships, the childhood skill now watches it for 24 hours by default instead of 30 minutes** (#6480). A full day catches slow npm registry updates, late CI and reports from users in other time zones. Checks are close together in the first hour, every 30 minutes until hour 6, then every 2 hours, with a final sweep at the 24-hour mark. A new problem brings that surface back to close checks until it settles. Between checks the agent uses a scheduled check or wake-up instead of holding a session open, and if it can't come back it reports the window as still open, not as clean.

name: v16.2.0
body:
### iMessage group chats

- **The iMessage group chat observer keeps Claude-Mem notes on a group chat** (#6457). Add a Photon iMessage line to the group and run `npx claude-mem imessage setup`. Each group chat gets its own Claude-Mem project with what the group decided, planned, asked for and shared, and who said what. It only reads: it never sends, reacts or changes a group. See [docs/imessage-group-observer.md](imessage-group-observer.md).

### iMessage on your Mac

- **Claude-Mem Messages, a Mac app that keeps notes on the iMessage chats you pick** (#6482). It lists your chats and group chats from the Messages app on your own Mac. Tick the ones to observe and write what to watch for in each ("plans and who's bringing what", "money: who paid, who owes"). New messages in those chats become notes in one Claude-Mem project per chat. It only reads: it never sends, reacts or changes a chat, and nothing is added to the group. Only new messages are read, from when it starts listening. The app needs Full Disk Access, and its setup screen walks you through turning it on. Download the unsigned build from the "iMessage Mac app" check, or build it with `integrations/imessage-mac/scripts/build-app.sh`. See [docs/imessage-mac-app.md](imessage-mac-app.md).
- **`claude-mem imessage mac` commands** do the same from Terminal: `check`, `chats`, `pick` (with `--focus` for what to watch for), `observe` and `contacts`.

## Security update for Next.js and React

This release moves the template to Next.js 16.4.6 and React 19.3.1, clearing every open `npm audit` and Dependabot advisory, including a remote code execution issue in `next/og`. If you started a project from the template, update your dependencies too.

### Highlights

name: v1.62.0
body:
### Minor Changes

- [#2588](https://github.com/mengxi-ream/read-frog/pull/2588) [`6e0f23e`](https://github.com/mengxi-ream/read-frog/commit/6e0f23efb2480e8d7e38f14bd5f4a34d8c60ef91) Thanks [@ananaBMaster](https://github.com/ananaBMaster)! - feat(hosted-ai): show a failed Built-in AI request's ID, with a button that copies it
  
  When a Built-in AI request fails, the error now shows its request ID with a copy button beside it. Put the ID in a bug report and we can find that exact request. It shows wherever the error does: the selection toolbar's translation and AI action panels, the word lookup card in video subtitles, the Translation Hub cards, the error card of a paragraph page translation could not translate, the error under a video's subtitles (with the ID in its tooltip), the failed video summary in the subtitles sidebar, and the message when a translated subtitles download fails. Input translation used to fail without a word when Built-in AI had a problem; it now says so in a message with the ID. Messages that already say what to do, such as log in, upgrade, quota used up or try another model, show no ID, and neither do errors from your own API keys or the free translation services.

- [#2580](https://github.com/mengxi-ream/read-frog/pull/2580) [`bc7e1c2`](https://github.com/mengxi-ream/read-frog/commit/bc7e1c25055ff590949b28f33a16c3d6fce6c80b) Thanks [@ananaBMaster](https://github.com/ananaBMaster)! - feat(options): add a Usage page with your plan and AI quota, and open settings on Preference
  
  Settings now has a Usage page, first in the sidebar. It shows your account and plan, your Built-in AI quota and your AI subtitles quota in one place. Pro and Ultra subscribers get a Manage subscription button. A free account gets an Upgrade button, and someone not logged in gets a Log in button with a note that logging in gives free AI quota every week. The quota sections on the API Providers and Video Subtitles pages moved here. With video subtitles turned off in simple mode, the page leaves out the AI subtitles quota. Opening settings now lands on Preference instead of API Providers.

- [#2578](https://github.com/mengxi-ream/read-frog/pull/2578) [`2f8e5ae`](https://github.com/mengxi-ream/read-frog/commit/2f8e5ae53152bcb161a4fd7bdf904f9fadf7c3a5) Thanks [@ananaBMaster](https://github.com/ananaBMaster)! - feat(options): add simple mode to turn off the features you don't use
  
  A new Simple mode page under Advanced in the options has a switch for each feature: Custom AI Actions, Page Translation (and its Hover translation), Video Subtitles, Input Translation, Floating Button, Selection Toolbar (and its Word annotation, Selection translation with Note suggestions, and Speak), Context Menu, Translation Hub and Glossary. A feature you turn off is as if it weren't installed: it no longer shows on web pages and its shortcuts do nothing. Its settings are kept, so turning it back on brings everything back as it was. Its pages leave the options sidebar, except the Custom AI Actions page and Page Translation's pages. Page Translation's pages stay because selection translation, input translation and the Translation Hub use its prompts, translation queue and cache. The popup has a new Simple mode button at the top that opens the same switches. With Page Translation off, the popup hides its page translation controls, and the context menu has no item to translate the page. A click on the floating button, when it is set to translate the page, then shows a message beside it that Page Translation is turned off in Simple mode, with a button that goes to its switch. A message beside a button near the edge of the page, such as the floating button's, no longer shrinks to a narrow column. With Custom AI Actions off, the selection toolbar, its ⋮ menu and the context menu no longer show AI actions, and on the Shortcuts page their keys show a Turn on link. The ⋮ button in the selection toolbar now only shows when its menu has something in it. The Enable switches at the top of the feature pages are gone, because Simple mode has them now, and a link to turn a feature on, such as on the Shortcuts page, goes to its switch there. The hide menus of the selection toolbar and the floating button now also name Options → Simple mode as a place to turn them back on. Turning off the whole selection toolbar, here or by hiding it on all sites, now also turns off its shortcuts; hiding it until reload or on one site keeps them. The popup no longer has its own Discord and blog buttons: What's New is now the first item under More, with a dot when there is a post you haven't read, and Discord is still under More.

### Patch Changes

- [#2566](https://github.com/mengxi-ream/read-frog/pull/2566) [`0e67035`](https://github.com/mengxi-ream/read-frog/commit/0e67035564bf9e026dbdc626ef4f87884f99edb4) Thanks [@ananaBMaster](https://github.com/ananaBMaster)! - feat(built-in-ai): run Built-in AI on Claude Haiku 5.5 instead of GPT-6 Luna
  
  New installs start every Built-in AI feature on Claude Haiku 5.5. When you update, every feature, selection toolbar action, language detection and Translation Hub card that runs on GPT-6 Luna moves to Claude Haiku 5.5, including ones you picked yourself. A Translation Hub card for GPT-6 Luna merges into an existing Claude Haiku 5.5 card. Features on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, GPT-6.2 Sol, Claude Sonnet 5.5 or your own providers stay where they are. A reasoning level you set for GPT-6 Luna does not carry over: Claude Haiku 5.5 starts on its own default, and switching back to GPT-6 Luna brings back its level.
